speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to understand the nature of the skin lesion you are concerned about to determine if it has any oncologic implications. Can you describe the lesion's appearance, including its size, shape, color, and if it has changed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of heavy smoking and the location of the lesion on the penile shaft, have you noticed any bleeding, pain, or ulceration in that specific area, and does the lesion on your finger look identical?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Digit). The presence of non-healing, painless, crusty lesions in a heavy smoker, particularly on the penile shaft and acral sites (fingers), strongly suggests Squamous Cell Carcinoma, which can be associated with smoking and chronic irritation.
